category_title: Student with developmental delay and learning disabilities exhibiting disruptive behaviors and repetitive questioning
minimal_context: The student is asked to complete two-digit addition problems during a whole-class math instruction time.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Please complete the two-digit addition problems on your worksheet.

STUDENT: (Looks anxious) I don't know how to do this.

TUTOR: Just try your best to answer them.

STUDENT: (Looks ashamed of herself for not performing well) It's too hard, I can't do it.

TUTOR: Keep looking at the numbers and try again.

STUDENT: (Feels unhappy and becomes disorderly and unsettled, pushing the materials away) No!

options.A: Prompt the student to call on a neighbor, ask a friend, or poll the class for help.
options.B: Provide individual academic supports and instruction, including prompting and coaching on the addition worksheet.
options.C: Provide an alternative kit comprising assorted coloring sheets, art materials, and crayons for the student.
options.D: Explain the math concept, demonstrate the addition principle, or model the academic skill for the student.
